title: Beyond Marginal Distributions: A Framework to Evaluate the Representativeness of Demographic-Aligned LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-simulated survey responses (via persona prompting and demographic fine-tuning) to human ground-truth data from the World Values Survey for Liberal and Conservative subgroups using marginal dissimilarity and higher-order correlation structures.

Comparing LLM-simulated survey responses to human ground-truth data from the World Values Survey for German, US American, Latin American, and Middle Eastern subgroups using marginal dissimilarity and higher-order correlation structures.
Comparing LLM-simulated survey responses to human ground-truth data from the World Values Survey for Male and Female subgroups using marginal dissimilarity and higher-order correlation structures.

Comparing LLM-simulated survey responses to human ground-truth data from the World Values Survey for different age subgroups (e.g., people over 30, old people) using marginal dissimilarity and higher-order correlation structures.
Evaluating recency and primacy effects by randomly flipping the response scale ordering for 50% of the multiple-choice prompts and comparing the normalized mean output distributions.
